reason: The cited evidence supports the Sabatier principle (E3) and shows synergistic activity in a multimetal catalyst (E4), but no passage demonstrates that isolated noble metal sites with adjacent non-noble metals cause charge transfer that tunes adsorption energies to the Sabatier optimum, nor that this mechanism enhances activity/selectivity. E1 even cautions against using the d-band center as a single descriptor. The key mechanistic premises are therefore largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Isolated noble metal sites in proximity to non-noble metals facilitate charge transfer
Charge transfer tunes adsorption energy of intermediates toward the Sabatier optimum
Tuning adsorption energy enhances catalytic activity and selectivity
The d-band center model explains the change in adsorption energy
The effect is general for multimetal catalysts under electrocatalytic conditions
